These are public immutable inputs for native package metadata, snapshot, and
migration tests. The component is the maintained captured current Java writer
`sha256:05e8bbaa90168aa250d779431a317fcde8f785d93e511054e0d5facaaad5787d`
(1,050,523 bytes), produced from the `eba0d96e` compiler-input source. Its exact
source, schema, codec, companion, HTTP marker, requirements, WIT and package
layers are retained with the hashes in `inputs.json`.

The tests assemble distinct package subjects and sign them with newly generated
test keys. The captured Java provenance model is descriptive input to that test
trust, with its package-input material rebound to each actual new package. This
is neither another Java compiler run nor a guest execution or distribution
qualification. No private key, credential, store, or runtime receipt is included.

The state schema and legacy package recipe layers come directly from the
unchanged committed `contracts/state` definitions. The current protected
migration recipe remains the separate installed core producer. Existing snapshots
keep their original mandatory artifact closure; newly produced snapshots also
carry the exact authenticated canonical package association required by migration.
